newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean 3-yr yields close flat, CDs fall.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean 3-yr yields close flat, CDs fall.

text.p: Yields on three-year corporate bonds closed flat with many investors being sidelined after a long Chusok holiday, dealers said. The debt market resumed trading on Monday after the Korean Thanksgiving holidays, which began Thursday last week.
They forecast the corporate yield would drift sideways this week in the absence of specific buying interest.
Yields on benchmark three-year corporate bonds closed flat on Monday with no specific buying interest, dealers said.
"Many investors are still in a post-Chusok holiday mood. There were no substantial buying or selling interest shown today," said a LG Securities dealer.
The market was closed for the Korean Thanksgiving holidays from last Thursday.
"Only investment trust companies and some insurers showed very lukewarm buying interest," said a hyundai Securities dealer. "The market will remain quiet throughout this week."

But dealers forecast the three-year yield would rise next week, given a large amount of new bond issues planned for October. The Korea Securities Dealers Association approved 2.87 trillion won worth of corporate bond issues next month against 1.95 trillion in September.

The Hyundai Securities dealer predicted the corporate yield would reach the 12.50 level by mid-October. But the LG Securities dealer said the yield would fall as institutional buying power showed signs of improvement in line with easing liquidity.
Dealers said the overnight call rate would fall to 17 percent level this week.
